## Where the tool does not do what the requirements say

Every row marked `‼`, except the four costs the criteria already accept — the two collateral limits and the two flatpak ones, recorded in [Where the tool does not yet meet these requirements](../planning/package-sync-conformance-criteria.md#where-the-tool-does-not-yet-meet-these-requirements) and not repeated here. Everything below is new against that section.

Each entry was found by one reading of the code and then put to an independent reader asked to refute it; what survived is what appears here, in the narrower wording that pass produced. None was observed on a running machine unless the entry says so, so each states what the code does, not what a run was seen to do.

**A14, A15 — apt offers to remove software it does not own.** `AptProbe.capture_source_items` drops packages installed from no configured repository and says the exclusion "happens HERE and nowhere else"; `AptProbe.query_target_items` applies no equivalent filter. A package installed from a downloaded `.deb` is therefore missing from Atlas's manifest and present in Nomad's, and diffs as a removal — whether both machines have it (A14) or only Nomad does (A15). `PKG-FR-DEB-OWNERSHIP` says `apt_sync` produces no item for such software in any configuration, which is the more specific rule and settles A15 against `PKG-FR-APT-REMOVE`'s general one; `PKG-FR-APT-SAME` independently rules out A14. The fix is one filter, and it costs a batched `apt-cache policy` over Nomad's manual set, which no run currently issues.

**C50, N12 — a repository can be deleted while the package that needs it stays.** `PKG-FR-REPO-DELETE` counts what still uses a repository "after this run's **approved** removals". `AptSyncJob` builds that set from the plan-time package diffs — the **proposed** removals — and `diff_apt_sources`'s own docstring says so. Nothing re-checks at converge. Approving a repository's deletion while declining its package's removal leaves the package installed with its origin gone. `flatpak_sync` counts against the machine's real state after its converge loop; apt has no equivalent.

**A62, A63 — a vendor build against a distribution build is never reported.** `origins.is_origin_mismatch` returns true only when both machines have a non-empty vendor origin set, and `OriginClassifier.classify` builds each as that machine's origins minus its own distribution origins. A copy served by the Ubuntu archive therefore has an empty set and the comparison short-circuits, so the case falls through to the version comparison — and produces no item at all when the two versions match. This is the worked example the user requirements give for two different pieces of software: `gh` from GitHub's repository against `gh` from Ubuntu's archive. `PKG-FR-DISTRO-ORIGIN` makes the distribution one origin per machine; the code treats it as no origin, which suppresses more than the mirror exemption buys.

**J115 — the Ubuntu Pro payload reaches the debug log.** `PKG-FR-ESM-PRIVACY` allows only whether Nomad is attached to be logged or shown. `AptProbe.target_pro_attached` issues `pro status --format json` through `RemoteExecutor.run_command`, which calls `_trace_output` unconditionally and emits `stdout: %s` at DEBUG — subscriber identity included — before `esm_gate` ever parses it. The existing test passes because its executor is a mock.

**K88 — the snippet registry is mirrored outside its own consent.** The registry lives at `~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml`, beside the decision files, but `folder_sync`'s non-overridable exclusion is the glob `*.decisions.yaml`, which does not match it. Wherever `~/.config` is a synced folder, `folder_sync` carries the registry Atlas→Nomad after the package jobs have run — the transfer `PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT` exists to gate, and one `PKG-FR-OUTCOME-SKIPPED` and `PKG-FR-NO-TERMINAL` both say must not happen when the job was skipped.

**C7 — files apt ignores are synced as pins and configuration.** Measured on this machine (apt 2.8.3, Ubuntu 24.04): `man 5 apt_preferences` requires files in `preferences.d` to carry no extension or `pref`, `man 5 apt.conf` requires no extension or `conf`, and `Dir::Ignore-Files-Silently` skips `~`, `.disabled`, `.bak`, `.dpkg-[a-z]+`, `.ucf-[a-z]+`, `.save`, `.orig` and `.distUpgrade` in all of them. `AptProbe.capture_dir_digests` passes an extension filter for `sources.list.d` alone, so a `99-vendor.bak` in `preferences.d` becomes an always-synced write from Atlas and an offered deletion on Nomad, though apt reads it on neither. `PKG-FR-APT-IGNORES` forbids treating such a file as configuration in any of add, change or remove.

**B27 — a hold outlives its package's mark and freezes a package that is not there.** `filter_inert` drops a marked package from Atlas's manifest, but the hold sets are read raw and `_drop_inert_diffs` looks up the hold's own id (`apt:hold:<name>`) against a mark recorded under `apt:package:<name>`. The hold item survives; `PackageConverger._hold_refusal` finds no package diff, reads that as "Nomad already has it", and runs `apt-mark hold` for a package Nomad does not have. That is the bookkeeping hold `PKG-FR-APT-HELD-TARGET` calls harmful, and it blocks every later attempt to install the package.

**K82 — data for a revision that did not converge is mirrored anyway.** `snap_sync_exclude_paths()` keeps each app's current-revision directory and excludes the rest, computed from Atlas's filesystem alone. It takes no decisions and no converge results, so where a revision change was declined or failed, `folder_sync` still writes Atlas's current-revision data into `~/snap/<app>/<atlas-revision>` on Nomad, whose snapd never installed it. The function's docstring states the assumption that makes the exclusion safe — that `snap_sync` converged the revision first — and a declined or failed item is exactly what breaks it. `PKG-FR-SNAP-DATA-BOUNDARY` forbids the result.

**K81 — with `snap_sync` off, every revision's data is mirrored.** The snap filters are emitted only when `_package_job_enabled("snap_sync")` holds, and that returns false both when the job is disabled and when the sibling map is absent. Nothing unconditional names anything under `~/snap`. `folder_sync` module's own comment records this as a deliberate trade, so it is a conflict between a documented choice and `PKG-FR-SNAP-DATA-BOUNDARY` rather than an oversight.

**B28 — a held package with no captured version installs unpinned.** `_plan_packages` admits a name into `_held_versions` only when a non-empty version was captured, and `PackageConverger._install` falls back to an unpinned `install_args([name])` otherwise, so `_held_version_refusal` is never reached and the package is frozen at whatever Nomad offered. `PKG-FR-APT-HOLD-VERSION` forbids the fallback. Reachability is not established by reading the code: the empty version is a defensive default, and `dpkg-query`'s measured non-zero exit on an unknown name would fail the job first.

**G72 — a registry entry's authoring record is overwritten without asking.** `_guard_registry_overwrite` compares bodies alone, while a `Snippet` also carries `label`, `authored_at` and `authored_on`, all of which the whole-file transfer replaces. `PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT` gates a transfer that would "lose or change an entry the target holds". What is lost is metadata — the replayed body stays byte-identical — so the consequence is narrow.

**H167 — the article overstates the automation hatch.** `PKG-NG-AUTOMATION-ENV` says a permanent answer given through the environment variable writes "a machine-specific mark **or an install snippet**". `_decisions_from_automation` returns decisions only, so `ReviewOutcome.snippets` is always empty on that path and no snippet can be authored through it. `review.py`'s own docstring already states the narrower, correct version, so this is the article to fix, not the code.

**A40 — the credential in an apt origin is never withheld.** `PKG-FR-CREDENTIAL-PRIVACY` requires the userinfo to be withheld wherever the system puts a URL in front of the user, and `ItemDiff` runs `redact_credentials` over every label and detail to do it. But `messages.display_origin` strips the scheme before the string becomes a detail, and `redaction.redact_credentials` returns early unless the text contains `://` — so for every origin line the redaction is a no-op. Measured here:

```
raw redacted   : https://***@repo.example.test/apt
display+redact : bearer:s3cr3ttoken@repo.example.test/apt
```

Every builder in `messages.py` that calls `display_origin` is affected — `build_origin_detail`, `build_repo_unavailable_detail`, `build_origin_mismatch_detail`, `build_origin_refusal_detail`. The builders that use the raw URI, `build_repo_removal_detail` and `build_stranded_repository_line`, still redact correctly. A private repository carries its password in its own address, so this is the case the article was written for.

**C81, C174 — a vendor's key rotation is never followed.** `PKG-FR-KEY-REFRESH` exempts a differing key only where "the target's own **distribution** packaging owns it". `AptProbe.capture_package_owned_keys` parses `dpkg --search` and discards the package names, and `Keyrings.manages` then exempts any owned path, so no distribution-versus-vendor distinction exists anywhere. A key a third-party vendor's own package placed on Nomad is left stale, and the rotation the user has on Atlas never arrives.

**D39, D40, D41, D71 — apply-time collateral is refused where it should be asked, in two of three places.** `LateCollateral.ensure_asked` is real and wired into `AptSyncJob._build_work`, and it does put the three-way question before the first install — but only for an approved install that plan time could not rehearse because this run writes its repository. Collateral the real transaction reveals in `PackageConverger._install`, and the whole removal direction — `remove` has no late path at all — reach a bare `ConvergeItemFailed` instead. `PKG-FR-COLLATERAL-MANUAL` requires consent to the consequence, and `PKG-FR-ASK-AGAIN` permits the second question; nothing is lost either way, but the user is told rather than asked. (`OriginClassifier.target_resolvable`'s docstring still describes the behaviour before `LateCollateral` existed.)

**E115 — the same data-boundary defect as K82, reached by a declined install.** Where a snap's install is declined rather than its revision change, `folder_sync` still mirrors that snap's current-revision directory. One root cause — `snap_sync_exclude_paths()` reads Atlas's filesystem and takes no decisions and no outcomes — so one fix closes both and neither closes alone.

**F79 — the verification refusal names no URL.** `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-INSTALL-ORIGIN` says either origin failure must name both URLs. Only the URL-mismatch branch of `_origin_refusal` does; the branch for a remote that has stopped verifying signatures names the settings alone. That branch runs only once the URLs already matched, so what is missing is the one shared URL — the reader is told a setting differs without being told which repository it is about.

**F146 — a remote that stops verifying mid-run is invisible.** `_installed_origin_refusal` compares URL alone, so a verification setting that changes between the pre-install check and the read-back is never seen. It also resolves the landed origin against the cached `_target_remotes_now_by_id`, which nothing invalidates between the two, so the read-back re-reads the same snapshot: adding a verification comparison there would not close the window without a fresh read.

**G5 — a hand-`.deb` that apt marks automatic is never detected.** `PKG-FR-MANUAL-SCOPE` covers every installed version no configured repository supplies. `capture_source_items` feeds only the `apt-mark showmanual` names into the no-candidate scan, so such a package reaches no review and no snippet can be written for it. Whether `apt_sync` then offers to remove Nomad's copy depends on Nomad's own manual mark — the A14 case.

## Questions the requirements do not settle

Each is a place where two articles can both be satisfied only by choosing between them, or where the text does not reach the case. None is a defect until it is ruled on.

- **B41 — a hold added and its package removed in the same run.** Both can be approved, because Atlas can hold a package outside its own manual set. The code removes and then holds, leaving Nomad holding what it no longer has. The articles say the hold is decided separately from its software; they do not say what happens when the two answers contradict.  
  A: Most intuitive if packages and holds are presented together: hold is mentioned in the same question as the package. The decision on the package is applied to the hold as well.
- **C — the conflict question is gated on the proposed installs.** `PKG-FR-REPO-CONFLICT` says the question is raised only for a repository this run writes because an approved package comes from it, but the question must be asked before the approvals exist. The code uses the plan-time superset, so a file can be asked about and then not written. Nothing is written wrongly; no article covers the outcome.  
  A: Why "the question must be asked before the approvals exist"? PKG-FR-REPO-CONFLICT doesn't say that. Inventing a constraint that doesn't exist?
- **D47 — a mark recorded earlier in the same run.** `PKG-FR-COLLATERAL-MARKED` says such a mark must count and that the question must say the package is marked. The protection counts, but items are built before answers exist, so the question cannot name a same-run mark. Whether the second half is required is not decidable from the text.  
  A: "items are built before answers exist": this is an implementation choice, apparently not in line with requirements. Building the "items" and the questions is apparently not dynamic enough.
- **E — whether a warning satisfies "a run MUST name".** `PKG-FR-SNAP-SIDELOAD` requires a run to name the sideloads it found. They are named in a job warning, not in the review or the report. On the warning reading the branch is covered; on the report reading it is unmet.
  A: Sideloaded snaps do not need to be searched/found nor named. Update the user req doc, the conformance-criteria, code and any other doc.
- **F118 — the filter article's unscoped clause.** "No filter may be in force on a remote **this run provisions**" is scoped; "a remote the source does not restrict MUST NOT stay restricted on the target" is not. Read literally the second would require touching remotes no approved application needs, which `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-REMOTE-DERIVED` forbids. The code takes the narrow reading.  
  A: Make PKG-FR-FLATPAK-FILTER more precise: "a remote the source does not restrict MUST NOT stay restricted on the target" is only meant to be applicable for remotes that are needed by approved applications (or their dependencies).
- **F121 — a third-scope application and the remote count.** `PKG-FR-FLATPAK-THIRD-SCOPE` skips such an installation, but an application in it can still be the last user of a remote, and the parser cannot see it. Whether deleting that remote is acceptable is a decision, not a test.

So you are raising a problem that doesn't exist: third-scope app will never refer to a remote that we touch/need and we will never touch a remote that a third-scope app uses, because the third-scope app uses a third-scope remote.
- **G79 — a registry on Nomad that cannot be parsed.** It reads as empty, so a transfer that would lose every entry counts as additive and asks nothing. `PKG-FR-READ-FAILS-JOB` says silence must not be read as an empty set; whether an unparsable file is silence or data is not stated.

- **J — a plan of nothing but report-only findings.** `PKG-FR-NO-TERMINAL` makes a headless run report any job with a non-empty review as skipped. Two machines differing only in versions therefore produce a skipped job, though nothing was ever decidable. This follows the letter of the article.
  A: Modify PKG-FR-NO-TERMINAL:
    - "MUST treat every reviewable item as declined for this run": "declined" should be "skip once"? "Decline" is not vocabulary we use.
    - in "reviewable item" and "non-empty review", this must be interpreted as "where user needs to make a decision"; not "where presented to user".
    - I don't understand what "it still transfers no registry" does here.
- **K23 — `folder_sync`'s exclusions depend on which package jobs are enabled.** `PKG-FR-JOB-INDEPENDENCE` says no job's behaviour may depend on whether another is enabled. The gating is deliberate and the reason is recorded in the code: a path hidden from the mirror while its own job is off is invisible to every mechanism at once. The article needs a clause either way.
  A: PKG-FR-JOB-INDEPENDENCE is only about package sync jobs. I just clarified that in the doc. Where do the requirements state that folder_sync depend on which package jobs are enabled? They don't. And the code doesn't either. See _decision_file_exclude_filters(). There is no problem.

python3 - <<'EOF'
import re
txt=open('docs/dev/package-sync-scenario-coverage.md').read()
lines=txt.split('\n')
# register entries
start=lines.index('## Gaps — what to test next')
end=lines.index('### What has no VM coverage at all')
reg=[]
for l in lines[start:end]:
    m=re.match(r'- \*\*([A-KN]\d+)\*\*', l)
    if m: reg.append(m.group(1))
print("register entries:", len(reg))
# marks
marks={}
for l in lines:
    if not l.startswith('| '): continue
    c=[x.strip() for x in l.strip().strip('|').split('|')]
    if len(c)<3: continue
    if re.fullmatch(r'[A-KN]\d+', c[0]): marks[c[0]]=c[-2]
from collections import Counter
print("register entry marks:", Counter(marks.get(r,'MISSING') for r in reg))
targets=[r for r,m in marks.items() if m in ('—','P')]
print("42 targets without register entry:", [r for r in targets if r not in reg])
print("register entries marked U/UV/V:", [r for r in reg if marks.get(r) in ('U','U V','V')])
EOF

        # Walk the cell left to right so a bare `::test_x` binds to the class named
        # nearest before it, not to whichever class the cell happens to end on.
        resolved: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
        current = previous[-1][0] if previous else ""
        for match in re.finditer(f"{CITATION.pattern}|{BARE_TEST.pattern}", cited):
            cls, fn, bare = match.group(1), match.group(2), match.group(3)
            if cls:
                current = cls
                resolved.append((cls, fn))
            elif current:
                resolved.append((current, bare))

        if not resolved and (same := SAME_AS.search(cited)) is not None:
            named = same.group(1)
            resolved = list(rows[named][2]) if named and named in rows else list(previous)

        rows[scenario] = (mark, cited, resolved)
        if resolved:
            previous = resolved
    return rows


def _tests() -> dict[tuple[str, str], set[str]]:
    """(Class, test) -> every scenario id any module's copy of it claims.

    Keyed without the module because the Test column often omits it, and a class and test
    name together are specific enough in practice. Where two modules share both — several
    have a `TestValidate` — their ids are pooled, which is the lenient direction.
    """
    found: dict[tuple[str, str], set[str]] = defaultdict(set)
    for path in sorted(TESTS.rglob("test_*.py")):
        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text())
        for node in ast.walk(tree):
            if not isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
                continue
            for item in node.body:
                if not isinstance(item, ast.FunctionDef | ast.AsyncFunctionDef):
                    continue
                doc = ast.get_docstring(item) or ""
                tag = DOCSTRING_TAG.match(doc)
                found[(node.name, item.name)] |= set(SCENARIO_ID.findall(tag.group(1))) if tag else set()
    return found


ROWS = _rows()
SUITE = _tests()


CLAIMED = sorted(sid for sid, (mark, _, _) in ROWS.items() if mark in COVERED)


def test_the_matrix_is_well_formed() -> None:
    """Every row carries five columns, a unique id and a coverage mark from the legend."""
    assert len(ROWS) > 1000, f"only {len(ROWS)} rows parsed — the table shape has changed"
    unknown = {sid: mark for sid, (mark, _, _) in ROWS.items() if mark not in COVERED | {"—", "‼"}}
    assert not unknown, f"coverage marks outside the legend: {unknown}"


def test_no_scenario_states_which_tier_proves_it() -> None:
    """The Scenario and Expected columns describe a situation and its outcome, not a test.

    Which tier proves a row is the Cov column's job, and saying it twice is how "on a VM"
    ends up in a sentence a reviewer is meant to set up by hand. Where a branch genuinely
    needs real package-manager behaviour, the Expected column says so by naming what a real
    run prints — `apt-get update` exiting 0, say — rather than by naming the test.
    """
    tiers = re.compile(r"\b(on a VM|VM run|integration test|unit test|mocked|a real run on a VM)\b")
    offenders: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in MATRIX.read_text().splitlines():
        if not re.match(r"^\| [A-KN]\d", line):
            continue
        cells = [cell.strip() for cell in line.strip().strip("|").split(" | ")]
        if len(cells) == 5 and (hit := tiers.search(f"{cells[1]} {cells[2]}")):
            offenders[cells[0]] = hit.group(0)
    assert not offenders, f"rows name a test tier in the Scenario or Expected column: {offenders}"


def test_every_claim_of_coverage_names_a_test() -> None:
    """A row claiming coverage must say which test proves it."""
    silent = [sid for sid in CLAIMED if not ROWS[sid][2] and sid not in COMPOSITIONS]
    assert not silent, (
        f"rows claim coverage but name no test: {silent}. Cite a `Class::test`, or list the row"
        f" in COMPOSITIONS where its branch holds only by reading two other rows together."
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scenario", CLAIMED)
def test_every_cited_test_exists(scenario: str) -> None:
    """A row claiming coverage must cite a test the suite actually has."""
    missing = [f"{cls}::{fn}" for cls, fn in ROWS[scenario][2] if (cls, fn) not in SUITE]
    assert not missing, f"{scenario} cites tests that do not exist: {missing}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("scenario", CLAIMED)
def test_every_cited_test_names_the_scenario_back(scenario: str) -> None:
    """The cross-reference runs both ways: a cited test carries the id that cites it.

    Without this, a scenario can be renumbered and every docstring left pointing at the
    branch that now holds its old number — which reads as coverage and is not.
    """
    citations = ROWS[scenario][2]
    if scenario in COMPOSITIONS or not citations:
        return
    if any(scenario in SUITE.get(key, set()) for key in citations):
        return
    named = [f"{cls}::{fn}" for cls, fn in citations]
    raise AssertionError(
        f"{scenario} is cited by no test that names it back."
        f" Put `{scenario}` at the start of the docstring of one of: {named}"
    )


def test_no_test_claims_a_scenario_the_matrix_does_not_have() -> None:
    """A docstring id that matches no row is a stale tag left by a renumbering."""
    orphans: dict[str, list[str]] = defaultdict(list)
    for (cls, fn), ids in SUITE.items():
        for sid in ids - set(ROWS):
            orphans[sid].append(f"{cls}::{fn}")
    assert not orphans, f"tests name scenarios the matrix does not define: {dict(orphans)}"

# Python Development Conventions

Apply to Python code/projects. New or owner-controlled projects: use defaults. Existing: follow project config (Python version, deps, tests, lint, CI) unless explicitly migrating. Use modern standards for supported version.

## Python Version and Modern Practices

- New Python projects: target >=3.14
- Existing projects: use modern syntax for configured version
- Use modern type syntax: e.g. `str | None` instead of `Optional[str]`, `list[str]` instead of `List[str]`
- Include `from __future__ import annotations` when improves annotation behavior for Python version
- Use `@override` for method overrides when available in Python version
- Prefer `StrEnum` for string-based enums when available in Python version
- Prefer `Path` from pathlib for local filesystem paths

## Project Setup and Developer Workflows

- MUST use uv for running code, managing dependencies in new projects
- Existing projects: use project's workflow. Don't replace Poetry/Hatch/tox/Makefiles unless asked
- Use plain uv commands: `uv sync`, `uv run ...`, `uv add`, etc. Avoid `uv pip`. NEVER use `uv pip install` unless project intentionally uses uv's pip-compatible interface
- Use `codespell` for checking typos in code/comments
- Use `ruff` for linting, formatting
- Use `basedpyright` for type checking
- Use `pytest` for testing

## Code Quality Standards

- Full type annotations for function signatures, modern syntax per Python version
- Import types from correct modules (e.g., use `collections.abc` not `typing` for collection types)
- Proper error handling with specific exception types, meaningful messages
- Single responsibility principle, keep functions focused
- Use context managers for resource management
- Prefer composition over inheritance
- Self-documenting code with meaningful names
- Follow PEP 8 (max 119 chars), use Python strengths, avoid anti-patterns

## Documentation Philosophy

- Document architectural decisions, design patterns
- Concise docstrings: focus on "why" not obvious "what"
- Explain complex logic rationales inline when needed
- Use backticks for variable/parameter names in docstrings
- Avoid repetitive or obvious comments

## Testing Strategy

- Small focused tests, clear locality. Use repo's layout (colocated, `tests/` tree, doctests)
- Avoid trivial tests that test language itself
- Simple assertions over complex pytest fixtures when possible
- Test edge cases, errors, boundary values
- Mock external dependencies, I/O operations appropriately
- Mocked integration behavior: add real-dep integration coverage where practical
- Never use `assert False` - raise `AssertionError` with explanation instead

## Performance Optimization Techniques

- Use appropriate data structures (sets for membership, deque for queues, etc.)
- Implement generators for memory-efficient iteration over large datasets
- Apply caching strategies where beneficial
- Utilize built-in functions/libraries (itertools, collections, functools)
- Consider algorithmic complexity, choose efficient algorithms
- Profile code using cProfile, line_profiler, or memory_profiler before optimizing

## Error Handling and Type Checking

- Use `# pyright: ignore` sparingly, always with explanation
- Raise `AssertionError` with descriptive messages for invariant violations
- Handle exceptions at appropriate levels, avoid bare except
- Use specific exception types that convey meaning

## File Operations Best Practices

- Prefer `Path` objects for local filesystem paths
- Atomic file writing for user data, config, state or other where partial output harmful
- Use context managers for file operations
- Handle encoding explicitly (default UTF-8)

## Core Principles

- Pragmatic: avoid over-engineering, premature optimization
- Leverage stdlib first. Use third-party packages sparingly
- Code clarity over clever tricks
- Aim for functional, clean, maintainable, performant code

# Python Development Commands

New or owner-controlled projects → uv. Existing repos → follow project's setup unless asked.

## Package Management with uv

Prefer uv (new projects). Skip `uv pip` unless project uses it. Don't replace other package managers without ask.

```bash
# Initialize new project
uv init

# Add dependencies
uv add package_name
uv add --dev ipykernel pytest ruff basedpyright  # dev dependencies

# Sync dependencies
uv sync

# Show installed packages
uv tree
uv tree --package package_name

# Run commands in virtual environment
uv run python script.py
uv run pytest
```

## Testing with pytest

```bash
# Run all tests
uv run pytest

# Run tests with coverage
uv run pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing

# Run specific test file or function
uv run pytest tests/test_module.py
uv run pytest tests/test_module.py::test_function

# Run tests matching pattern
uv run pytest -k "pattern"

# Run tests with verbose output
uv run pytest -v

# Run tests and stop on first failure
uv run pytest -x
```

## Linting and Formatting with ruff

```bash
# Format code
uv run ruff format .

# Check linting issues
uv run ruff check .

# Fix auto-fixable issues
uv run ruff check --fix .

# Check specific file
uv run ruff check path/to/file.py
```

## Type Checking with basedpyright

```bash
# Type check entire project
uv run basedpyright

# Type check specific file
uv run basedpyright path/to/file.py
```

## Code Quality Checks

```bash
# Run all quality checks (typical CI pipeline)
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run ruff check .
uv run basedpyright
uv run pytest

# Check for common typos
uv run codespell
```

## Profiling and Performance

```bash
# Profile with cProfile
uv run python -m cProfile -s cumtime script.py

# Profile with line_profiler
uv run kernprof -l -v script.py

# Memory profiling
uv run python -m memory_profiler script.py
```

## Common Development Patterns

```bash
# Check outdated packages
uv tree --outdated

# Clean pyc files and caches only when explicitly requested
find . -type d -name "__pycache__" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type d -name ".pytest_cache" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type d -name ".ruff_cache" -exec rm -rf {} +
find . -type f -name "*.pyc" -delete
```

content.content:
Removing a snap leaves snapd's own pre-removal snapshot in place — the only recovery path if the removal was a mistake.

### Refresh holds

Refresh holds replicate as their own items, both when added and when removed. A hold recorded for a snap the source no longer has produces no item.

### Sideloaded snaps

Snaps installed from a local `.snap` file are out of scope (#221). They are ignored on both machines: never installed, never removed, never an item. A run names the ones it found so the user knows they are unmanaged, and does nothing else about them.

## flatpak

flatpak follows the shape every job has: what the source has is offered for install, what only the target has for removal, what cannot be converged is reported. What is particular to flatpak:

### Identity

A flatpak application is identified by its **scope** and its **full reference including branch**. The same application in both scopes, or on two branches, is two independent items — one install and one removal — reported as found.

Origin is not part of that identity: flatpak refuses to install a reference already present from a different remote, so a difference of origin is reported rather than converged, and takes precedence over a version difference.
